newsitem.title: POLAND: OKOCIM TO LAUNCH NEW BEERS, RAISE OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: OKOCIM TO LAUNCH NEW BEERS, RAISE OUTPUT.

text.p: Poland's Okocim brewer, 33-percent owned by Denmark's Carlsberg , wants to raise its 1997 production by 9-10 percent to above 1.5 million hectolitres and launch new brands, Okocim's president said.

Mieczyslaw Mietla told reporters late on Friday at a promotion event for its new brand "browar", the firm would start producing licenced Carlsberg and Tuborg beer in its Brzesko brewery by mid-year at the latest.
"Okocim wants to keep its position on the Polish market. That is why we launch the 'browar' beer. We will also introduce non-returnable bottles, cans and four-packs," Mietla said.
"By mid-year at the latest we will start making licenced Carlsberg and Tuborg brands, which are now only available through imports," he said.
Mietla added the company will decide on the details of its investment programme, now consulted with Carlsberg, in the first half of this year.
